title: 赴英留学生的残酷现实（4）
desc: 赴英留学生的残酷现实（4）

paragraphs.en: The first thing that hit Ajith when he arrived was the cold. The second was the realisation that none of what he'd been told was true.
paragraphs.zh: 阿吉斯抵达时，首先感受到的是刺骨的寒冷，紧接着便意识到，之前听到的一切全是谎言。

paragraphs.en: He had not secured university accommodation, so he rented an Airbnb for the first fortnight while looking for a place to live. He quickly discovered that to rent property in the UK, you need payslips and references from a previous landlord. He had neither.
paragraphs.zh: 他没有申请到大学宿舍，所以前两周租了间爱彼迎，同时寻找住处。他很快发现，在英国租房需要工资单和前房东的推荐信，而他两样都没有。

paragraphs.en: Panicking, Ajith called the agent in India for advice. The agent told him to walk around the city to find "for rent" signs, and then blocked his number. "That's when I realised, they're giving fake promises and they're lying," said Ajith.
paragraphs.zh: 惊慌失措的阿吉斯打电话给印度的中介寻求建议。中介告诉他，在城里四处走走，寻找"出租"标志，然后挂断了他的电话。阿吉斯说："那时我意识到，他们是在做虚假承诺，他们在撒谎。"

paragraphs.en: In response to these claims, a spokesperson for StudyIn said: "We care deeply about the experience of every student, but equally we do not think it's reasonable to conclude anything about our service based on the unsubstantiated comments of one student dating from over five years ago."
paragraphs.zh: 针对这些说法，StudyIn的一位发言人表示：‘’我们非常重视每一位学生的体验，但同样认为，仅凭一名学生五年前未经证实的评论就对我们的服务下结论，是不合理的。”

paragraphs.en: For two months, Ajith bounced between Airbnbs, burning through his remaining loan money, until he managed to get a job at Aldi. Working 20 hours per week – the maximum his visa allowed – he earned £900 a month.
paragraphs.zh: 两个月来，阿吉斯辗转于多家爱彼迎民宿，花光了剩余的贷款，直到他终于在奥乐齐超市找到工作。每周工作20小时——这是他的签证允许的最长工作时间——他每月能赚900英镑。

paragraphs.en: He found a room. The rent was £650, which left £250 for everything else. "I was working for rent, basically," he said. "I worked hard for survival." Meanwhile, he was also trying to study.
paragraphs.zh: 他找到了一间房，月租650英镑，剩下的250英镑要应付其他所有开销。他说："基本上，我就是在为房租工作，为了生存而努力工作。"与此同时，他还要努力完成学业。

paragraphs.en: Sam had a better experience with his agent at Edvoy, and on his advice, he had secured accommodation in Dundee on SpareRoom before leaving India. As he settled into university life, making friends from all over the world, Sam quickly developed a taxonomy of his fellow international students.
paragraphs.zh: 山姆在Edvoy的留学中介那里获得了更好的体验，并在其建议下，离开印度前就在SpareRoom网站上预定了邓迪的住宿。随着他逐渐适应大学生活，并与来自世界各地的同学交上朋友，山姆很快对身边的国际生们形成了一套分类体系。

paragraphs.en: At one end were the wealthy, there for the experience. At the other were those who had no real interest in studying and only wanted to find paid work in the UK. In the middle – where Sam placed himself – were the middle-class strivers.
paragraphs.zh: 一端是富人，他们来是为了体验生活。另一端则是那些对学习毫无兴趣，只想在英国找份有偿工作的人。而夹在中间的——萨姆将自己归为此类——是那些努力奋斗的中产阶级。

paragraphs.en: "You're trying to take studies seriously but you also need money to get by," he said. Within weeks of arrival, he started applying for graduate trainee roles in finance, as well as part-time work in the corporate sector. He received blanket rejections.
paragraphs.zh: "你既想认真对待学业，又需要钱来维持生计，"他说。抵达后几周内，他开始申请金融领域的毕业生培训职位，以及企业部门的兼职工作。他收到了铺天盖地的拒绝信。

paragraphs.en: He lowered his expectations, applying for more junior corporate roles, and anything vaguely adjacent – customer service at a bank, assistant at an accountancy firm – but the rejections continued. "I was confused. I was overwhelmed," he said. "The job search was a full-time role in itself, and I had academic work. It was a really tough time."
paragraphs.zh: 他降低了期望，申请了更多初级的企业职位，以及任何稍微沾边的工作——银行的客服、会计公司的助理——但拒绝依然接踵而至。“我很困惑，感到不知所措，”他说，“找工作本身就像一份全职工作，而我还有学业要完成。那真是一段艰难的时期。”

paragraphs.en: The terms of Sam's loan left little room for things to go wrong. "The cost of living was really, really high, and it felt like every month the expenses grew," he said. By Christmas, he was panicking. He broadened his search beyond corporate jobs, towards anything that would pay the bills.
paragraphs.zh: 山姆的贷款条件让他几乎没有出错的余地。他说："生活成本真的非常高，感觉每个月的开销都在增加。"到了圣诞节，他开始恐慌。他扩大了求职范围，不再局限于企业职位，而是寻找任何能支付账单的工作。

paragraphs.en: Eventually, through other international students, he found a string of part-time jobs – cashier at a sweet shop, flyering for a fish and chip shop, collecting glasses in a nightclub. "I had to work, so I just accepted it," he said. "But it was hard on my mental health."
paragraphs.zh: 最终，通过其他国际学生，他找到了一系列兼职工作——在糖果店当收银员、为炸鱼薯条店发传单、在夜店收杯子。"我必须工作，所以我只能接受它，"他说。"但这对我的心理健康造成了伤害。"

paragraphs.en: More than two-thirds of all full-time students in the UK now take on paid work during term-time. For international students, the financial pressure can be especially sharp.
paragraphs.zh: 在英国，超过三分之二的全日制学生现在会在学期期间从事有偿工作。对于国际学生来说，经济压力可能尤其大。

paragraphs.en: Some work cash in hand to get around the 20-hour limit imposed by their visa. Others travel long distances for menial work in factories or warehouses.
paragraphs.zh: 一些人为规避签证对工作时长的限制，选择打零工，还有一些人则长途跋涉，在工厂或仓库从事卑微的工作。

paragraphs.en: In December 2024, a group of five Indian students living in Leicester were involved in a car accident as they drove home at 5.45am from a night shift at a warehouse.
paragraphs.zh: 2024年12月，五名居住在莱斯特的印度学生于凌晨5点45分下夜班后驾车回家，途中遭遇车祸。

paragraphs.en: Chiranjeevi Panguluri, a 32-year-old master's student, was killed instantly, and two of the other students in the car were seriously injured.This was an exceptional tragedy, but the work this group of students was doing was not unusual.
paragraphs.zh: 32岁的研究生奇兰杰维·潘古里当场死亡，车上另外两名学生受重伤。这是一场特殊的悲剧，但这群学生所做的工作并不特殊。

paragraphs.en: On social media, there is a whole genre of videos made by Indian students in the UK showcasing "a day in the life" of their work in Amazon or Evri warehouses.
paragraphs.zh: 在社交媒体上，有一类由在英印度学生制作的视频，专门展示他们在亚马逊或Evri仓库"一天的工作生活"。

paragraphs.en: "This is how student life goes," says one young man, auto-dubbed in English, as he films himself starting a night shift at DPD. He describes his schedule that day: up at 6am, leaving the house at 8am for university, getting home at 4.30pm, sleeping until 6pm, cooking dinner, before leaving for a night shift that will run from 11pm until 4am.
paragraphs.zh: "这就是学生生活，"一位年轻人在DPD开始夜班时，用自动配音的英语对着镜头说道。他描述了当天的日程：早上6点起床，8点出门去大学，下午4点半到家，睡到6点，做晚饭，然后开始从晚上11点到凌晨4点的夜班。
